headline: Gemini 4 drops another flavor: Neon
summary: Only one thing worth your time today: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, and the pricing is kind of a mess.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon is out
items.pitch: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon. It's pitched as fast, cheap, and good at following tricky instructions. People on HN are talking about it a lot.
why: Josh Woodward says it follows instructions well and is faster and cheaper
HN gave it 867 points and 686 comments, so lots of people are watching
Simon Willison tested it: its image drawing beats Hydrogen but loses to Carbon
actions: Switch to Neon in the Gemini app and try it on a pay analysis task you do often
Run the same task on Claude and Gemini and compare the results
deep_dive: Gemini 4 now comes in three tiers: Carbon, Neon, and Hydrogen. Neon sits in the middle, a trade-off between speed and cost.
The pricing is a mess: Neon costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 for output. Carbon is half price right now, at $2/$10, but goes up to $4/$20 starting December 1.
Simon says Neon makes the pricing even more confusing, so don't just go by price. Try it yourself first.
items.signals: HN 867 points · 686 comments · Simon Willison's hands-on test · Announced by Josh Woodward

items.title: Putting an agent in an outside sandbox
items.pitch: Simon Willison built a "sandbox on the outside" setup that lets Claude Code and Codex run code more safely.
why: The agent's code runs in an isolated environment, so if it screws up or gets prompt-injected, your computer is safe
You can limit which websites it can reach, and you don't have to hand your keys straight to the agent
items.signals: Posted by Simon Willison on November 17 · Built with Prime Radiant · Three sandbox implementations

still_tracking.name: GPT-6.2 Astra / Sol
